Hi Julia / ACME legal team —

Thanks for the note and the questions. Short answers up front:

- Role: Redwood will be contracting as Processor for the pilot. Module Two (Controller-to-Processor) is the appropriate module for the EU SCCs.
- UK transfers: Redwood uses the UK International Data Transfer Addendum (UK IDTA) alongside the EU 2021 SCCs when the data subject's location is the UK. We can either:
  a) Execute the EU 2021 SCCs (Module Two) plus the UK IDTA as an addendum, or
  b) Execute the standalone UK version if you prefer separate paperwork for UK transfers.

Our standard practice is option (a) — EU 2021 SCCs (Module Two) + UK IDTA addendum, executed in a single DocuSign package. That keeps versioning and obligations aligned.

A few operational notes for your counsel:
- Signatories: Redwood requires an authorized signatory on the signature page (our standard template names "Redwood Inference, Inc."). If ACME needs a specific signatory name/role on our side, let us know.
- Technical/organizational measures: we'll include a redwood_sccs_attachment describing our processor controls and the relevant subprocessor list per your intake form.
- Minimal redlines: we cannot accept broad customer obligations that re-assign processor responsibilities to Redwood, or requests to remove our ability to engage subprocessors under a standard notification model.

I have attached our execution template for SCCs (standard Module Two signature page and redwood controls stub). If your counsel is happy with option (a) we can proceed to DocuSign and target execution within 48-72 hours.

Attachments: RDW_SCC_template_v3.pdf

Regards,
Irene Choi
Lead Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
